entries.title: Enhancing KV Cache Efficiency with Compression and Bit-Plane Eviction in Transformer Models
subheads: Undergraduate Research Program, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute
meta: Advisor: Prof. Tong Zhang; Mentor: Dr. Rui Xie
bullets: Profiled KV-cache memory growth in LLaMA 3.1 8B inference, characterizing FP16 cache footprint at approximately 128 KB per token and 1 GB for an 8K-token context.
Designed a memory-budgeted KV-cache retention policy combining semantic clustering with temporal recency to prioritize important context tokens under constrained cache capacity.
Prototyped token-to-cluster mapping and lookup mechanisms to support efficient assignment and retrieval of retained KV-cache entries during autoregressive decoding.
Evaluated memory-quality tradeoffs by comparing semantic-temporal retention against recency-based retention and bit-plane precision-reduction baselines.

entries.title: GPU Memory Management for High-Throughput LLM Serving
subheads: Undergraduate Research Program, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute
bullets: Investigated GPU memory fragmentation in vLLM-style LLM serving, focusing on how PagedAttention maps logical KV-cache blocks to non-contiguous physical GPU memory during large-batch autoregressive inference.

Developed PyTorch-based profiling scripts to sweep sequence length, request concurrency, and KV block size across synthetic serving workloads, targeting 128-2048 token contexts and 1-64 concurrent requests.

Benchmarked contiguous over-provisioning against block-based KV-cache allocation to quantify internal fragmentation, reserved-token waste, and effective GPU memory utilization under variable-length prompts and outputs.
Analyzed vLLM's request scheduling path across waiting, running, and swapped queues, identifying how CPU/GPU block allocation, preemption, and block reuse affect throughput under GPU memory pressure.

entries.title: Huichuang Medical Equipment

Authored a 30,000-word Chinese technical manual covering theoretical circuit analysis, calibration protocols, operation procedures, and QA workflows to support product transfer and internal standardization.

entries.title: SRAM-Based 4-bit MAC Accelerator
subheads: ESE 5700 Digital Integrated Circuits; Cadence Virtuoso, Spectre, Pegasus, Quantus, Python
bullets: Designed a transistor-level SRAM-fed MAC accelerator in 18 nm FinFET, integrating two custom 16 × 4 6T SRAM macros, a 4 × 4 unsigned multiplier, a 12-bit accumulator, and a pipelined sequencer; computes a 16-element dot product in 17 cycles at a 3.2 ns clock (54 ns latency, 19 pJ, 4.5 × 10³ µm²) at 0.8 V, TT.

Sized the 6T bitcell through hand analysis and a cell-ratio sweep, then drew DRC/LVS-clean custom bitcell and mirrored array layouts with Quantus extraction; achieved post-layout hold/read SNM of 0.28/0.14 V and a 0.24 V write margin, with the cell remaining functional down to 0.5 V.

Built the synchronous SRAM macro: registered inputs, a flat NAND4 row decoder chosen over a predecoded design via logical-effort comparison (22% lower core delay), precharge/equalization, tri-state write drivers, full-swing read path with output latch, and a 64-stage delay-chain controller generating precharge, wordline, write, and sense pulses; reached 1.2 ns read access and a 3.2 ns minimum period.

Derived wordline pulse budgets from extracted bitline load and cell current (0.47 ns read, 0.18 ns write) and verified every control-edge ordering margin, including a passing run with 20% added bitline capacitance.

Designed a transmission-gate master-slave register with a shared nonoverlapping clock generator; characterized clock-to-Q, polarity-dependent setup/hold, clock capacitance, and clock energy under both the 9-register SRAM and 21-register MAC clock fanouts.

Implemented the datapath as a NAND2-based array multiplier and a 12-bit ripple-carry adder; calibrated a logical-effort model from FO1/FO4 simulations and upsized 22 carry-path gates, reducing adder delay by 8.5% with the predicted improvement within 7 ps of simulation.

Designed the sequencer (one-hot FSM, 4-bit counter, and pipeline-control registers) to overlap SRAM reads with accumulation, with synchronous reset, mid-computation restart, external load muxing, and accumulator clear/load/hold implemented through data-input selection rather than clock gating.

Closed system timing: the hand-estimated 2.0 ns SRAM-to-accumulator critical path matched the 2.1 ns measured arrival; a clock-period scan showed the limit was SRAM write-off-to-precharge ordering rather than the datapath (1.1 ns slack); hold was checked on all 39 DFFs, all with positive margin.

Automated verification with Python-driven Spectre flows (stimulus generation, waveform grading, setup/hold boundary searches, period scans) across exhaustive multiplier tests, 384 datapath vectors, block-level unit tests, and full-system test vectors plus reset/restart sequences, all passing.

Measured energy with separate supply probes per block: 1.2 pJ/MAC including memory and 0.45 pJ/MAC excluding it, with SRAM consuming 62%; estimated area with a bitcell-calibrated density method, showing periphery dominates at this array size.

entries.title: Out-of-Order Processor and Memory System Design
subheads: ECSE 4780 Advanced Computer Hardware Design; SystemVerilog, ModelSim, Intel Quartus Prime Lite
bullets: Implemented a modular SystemVerilog out-of-order processor datapath with two-wide dispatch, RAT-backed register renaming, an 8-entry reorder buffer, reservation stations, load-store queue, multi-cycle functional units, common data bus writeback, and backend resource backpressure.

Designed precise commit and recovery logic supporting in-order retirement, completion tracking, exception recognition, trap visibility at the ROB head, younger-instruction flush across ROB/RS/LSQ/RAT state, late-result masking, and retirement-time store commit.

Built and verified memory-system RTL including an 8 KiB direct-mapped write-back/write-allocate cache with FSM-based miss handling and a two-core MESI coherence model with private L1 caches, shared-bus transactions, L2 responses, and ModelSim testbenches covering dependency, scheduling, cache, coherence, and exception cases.

entries.title: RISC-V Processor RTL Design and Pipeline Hazard Control
subheads: SystemVerilog, ModelSim 20.1, Intel Quartus Prime Lite, RV32I Datapath and Control
bullets: Implemented RV32I processor RTL across single-cycle, multi-cycle, and five-stage pipelined datapaths, integrating instruction decode, immediate generation, ALU control, register-file access, PC update logic, load/store paths, and branch/jump handling.

Designed FSM-based control and pipeline hazard logic, including fetch/decode/execute/memory/writeback pipeline registers, forwarding, load-use stalls, branch/jump flushes, x0-safe dependency handling, and ModelSim testbenches for register, memory, control-flow, stall, and flush correctness.

entries.title: Embedded Robotic Control System on RPI-RSLK Platform
subheads: C, MSPM0G3507 LaunchPad, RPI-RSLK, GPIO, Timers, PWM, ADC, I2C, Encoders
bullets: Developed embedded C control software for the RPI-RSLK robotic car on the MSPM0G3507 LaunchPad, integrating GPIO, timer interrupts, PWM motor control, ADC-based potentiometer inputs, I2C sensor communication, encoder feedback, and H-bridge motor drivers.

Implemented and tuned motion-control routines for predetermined path following, remote speed/steering control, and gesture-based driving, using encoder-derived wheel measurements, differential motor control, heading estimation, and on-board hardware testing.
